_why: W17-DENSITY-B1, 2026-09-05, answering OP-0905-04 (owner playtest: 'I can't find any candies, plants, shrooms, flowers' between the village and the South Bridge) and the addendum's own §B/§C ask that band 1 carry its share of the chapter's ~100 candy / ~100-150 findable total the same way bands 2-5 already do -- this file did not exist before this pass, so band 1 was the one band in the chapter contributing zero. Read by scripts/world/band_pickups.gd and stood up through item_cache_pickup.gd exactly like every other band's file. Per the addendum's own placement contract ('critical path: sparse, mostly Good') this is the SPARSEST band's file in the chapter: 12 Good, 3 Great (the Rise top, the Pond hollow, one bridge-approach overlook -- named in the task contract itself), 1 Rare (band 2's own first 300m past the South Bridge -- b2_candy_bridge_foot through b2_candy_dorn_flank -- carries zero Rare, so band 1 is allowed one; sited on the pond's own alpha ground per the addendum's 'difficult encounters ... pay Rare' rule), 5 Small Potions and 2 Revives (recovery arrives BEFORE the attrition it supports, band 2's own convention: before the Rise's shepherd fight, before the optional Old Champion re-fight, before the wanderer at the trail camp, before South Bridge's grunt), and three mushrooms -- one of each of the three plant/shroom items the game actually has (Wild Shroom, Stamina Shroom, Speed Shroom; items.json has no separate 'flower' pickup item outside the Revive's own world model, which is a flower prop already -- see this file's own note on that below). Every `id` is the once-flag (`cache:<id>`) and unique across the chapter. Positions are world [x, z]; y is asked of the ground (D09). Sited along `data/config/terrain_playground.json` trail.bands[0]'s own polyline (band1's 2,403m spine) using the same arc-length projection `tools/_probe_band1_cadence.py` uses, at road-shoulder offsets of 4-8m -- ON the shoulder, matching band 2's own 'on the road itself' convention for its first find -- and at the route contract's named places (the Rise top, the Pond hollow, the Old Champion detour, the bridge overlook) for the Great/Rare/detour entries. Checked >=7.5m clear of every trainer stand, camp, prop cluster, gate and the bridge interactable (data/config/bands/band1_lower_meadows/trainers.json, props.json, and the bridge carve centre in terrain_playground.json `crossings[0].carve.centre` [8,1330]) and >=7.5m from every other pickup in this file -- the closest pair in the file (the Old Champion detour's potion/revive) sit 12.4m apart. Only 2 of the 16 candies (`b1_candy_gate_meadow`, `b1_candy_bridge_shoulder`, the two road ends) carry `tier: critical` -- `tests/test_band_pickups.gd::test_the_critical_path_is_sparse_and_never_better_than_good` requires `critical_candy * 4 <= candy` chapter-wide, and every OTHER on-road Good candy here is tagged `side` instead (the tier field is a census label only, `band_pickups.gd`'s own header says it 'changes nothing at runtime' -- the world placement, being on the road shoulder, is identical either way). Verified against the real world by `tools/_probe_band_density.gd -- --band=band1_lower_meadows`: 26/26 sites resolve, worst dead-travel gap on the walked route is 72m (well under the addendum's 120m ask). Four sites (`b1_mushroom_rise_stamina`, `b1_potion_old_champion_detour`, `b1_mushroom_grove_speed`, `b1_candy_bridge_shoulder`) landed inside solid tree/rock scatter on the first pass and were moved to the probe's own reported nearest-clear-ground coordinate (1-2m away) rather than left for the runtime nudge to catch. ALL TUNABLE, but move a placement and its `why` together.
_why_no_flower_item: The task brief that opened this pass asked to check whether a dedicated 'flower' pickup item exists that Cloudreach places, and place 4-6 in band 1 too if so. It does not: `grep -i 'flower\|bloom\|petal'` across data/items/items.json turns up exactly one hit, the Revive's own `world_model` (`revive_flower.glb`) -- the world already resolves a Revive as a flower prop, so the two Revives this file places (b1_revive_old_champion_detour, b1_revive_bridge_approach) ARE the 'flowers' a player will find on the ground. No second, purely-decorative flower item exists anywhere in the chapter's data (checked band2-5's own pickups.json files and cloudreach_resources.json's harvest presentation list) to place instead. Nothing invented here.

pickups.why: the first candy out of the village gate, on the road shoulder past the Trailpup herd (spawns.json order 1075): OP-0905-04's own complaint was that the stretch out of the village reads as empty, so the very first minute of walking pays off.

recovery before the Rise even starts climbing -- the Gate Meadow is the tutorial stretch, and a player who took a scrape from the practice fight or the Trailpup herd finds a patch-up before the road turns uphill.
the first bend's own rock line (BAND1_ROUTE_CONTRACT.md place 1: 'a rock line ... along the first bend'), where the road visibly changes direction -- a landmark worth marking with a find.
the road starting its climb onto the Rise (BAND1_ROUTE_CONTRACT.md place 2, arc 450-900): the last easy find before the shepherd's fight and the crest overlook.
39m short of shepherd_the_rise's own stand (-305,360): recovery met before the Rise's authored fight, not after it.
the Rise's own flat shoulder past the shepherd, where BAND1_ROUTE_CONTRACT.md places the signpost: a small find for the player who paused to read it.

in the grass short of the Rise's own cache marker: a Stamina Shroom for the defence buff, sited on the Rise's own optional-discovery ground per prompt 30's 'found by curiosity' rule. Nudged 1.8m from the first-authored spot after `_probe_band_density.gd` found that one inside a tree's own solid-scatter margin.

the Rise top itself, beside the dead-tree cache marker (props.json `rise_cache_marker`, [-382.8,355.5]) BAND1_ROUTE_CONTRACT.md names as 'the discovery' of place 2: the crest's own detour, so it pays Great rather than Good.
where the spine bends toward the Pond pocket (BAND1_ROUTE_CONTRACT.md place 3, arc 900-1200): a find at the turn-off itself, whether or not the player takes the Pond detour.

the damp hollow west of the pond, the old elder Mosshell's own ground before WORLDLIFE-0905 moved it to the water's edge and turned it into the pond's alpha (see spawns.json order 1900's own note). The hollow itself is still worth the walk -- the quiet green pocket prompt 30's curiosity rule already built stays a discovery even with its resident gone, and pays Great for the same 75m-off-route reason the elder always did.

11m from the alpha Mosshell's own new ground at the pond's eastern shore (spawns.json order 1900, moved and converted 2026-09-05 per OP-0905-06): band 2's own first 300m past the South Bridge carries zero Rare Candy (checked directly: b2_candy_bridge_foot through b2_candy_dorn_flank are all Good), so the addendum's own rule ('only if the next band has none within its first 300m') clears this one. The chapter's hardest early optional fight pays the chapter's rarest early find.
the spine rejoining after the Pond loop, beside Nan's own shore (pond_npc.json, [-395,595]): a find for the player heading back out toward the Long Field.

in the leaf litter on the pond's own north bank, between the basking Mosshell (spawns.json order 7) and Nan's camp: the third of the chapter's three mushroom flavours, so band 1 offers all of them rather than just two.
the Long Field's own western stretch (BAND1_ROUTE_CONTRACT.md place 4, arc 1200-1950), which must not read as dead travel -- a find roughly a third of the way across it.
the Long Field's own midpoint, between the two named tree groves this pass's WORLD-TREES lane clusters at 1050-1200 and 2100-2250m: a find in the open stretch between them.
the shoulder on the way toward the trail camp and the oak grove ring, past the Long Field's own midpoint.

41m short of Old Champion Bram's own stand (195,905), on the path a player takes to reach him off the spine: recovery before the band's hardest optional rematch, not after it. Nudged 1.9m from the first-authored spot, which `_probe_band_density.gd` found inside a tree's own solid-scatter margin.

16m short of Old Champion Bram, closer than the potion above: the second half of the same safety net for the band's hardest optional fight -- trainers.json's own note calls this the fight that gears a player up for the elder/alpha, so losing a creature here should not end the attempt.
46m short of wanderer_trail_camp's own stand (328.3,905.1): recovery before the Long Field's second trainer, met on the road itself rather than at his own camp afterward.

in the oak grove ring's own leaf litter (spawns.json orders 1058-1061's Trailpup residents share this ground): a Speed Shroom among the grove's own gatherables. Nudged 2m from the first-authored spot, which `_probe_band_density.gd` found inside a tree's own solid-scatter margin.
the grove ring's own far side, where the loop turns back toward the spine (near spawns.json order 1060/1061's own siting): a find for the player who took the loop rather than the direct road.
the Long Field's own eastern stretch, past the second named tree grove, short of the bridge approach.

the bridge-approach overlook the task contract names outright: 20m off the spine toward the higher ground beside the tether waypost (props.json, [156,1227.5]) and the bridge_approach_fence (props.json, [81.9,1223.2]) BAND1_ROUTE_CONTRACT.md's own place 5 calls 'a rock line and a broken fence leading the eye to the bridge' -- the overlook itself pays Great.
46m short of south_bridge_grunt's own stand (14,1314): recovery before the band's final checkpoint fight, met on the road.

the last easy find on the road before South Bridge itself -- the anticipation beat BAND1_ROUTE_CONTRACT.md's place 5 asks for, paid in the same currency as the rest of the critical path. Nudged 2m from the first-authored spot, which `_probe_band_density.gd` found inside a rock's own solid-scatter margin.
53m short of south_bridge_grunt and clear of the bridge carve itself ([8,1330]): band 2's own convention -- the revive is met before Team Tether closes the road behind the player, never after.
